question: Which historical figure is the Santosh Trophy, launched in 1941, named after?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhury**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Santosh Trophy, launched in 1941, is named after **Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhury**, the Maharaja of Santosh, a region in present-day Bangladesh.
 
• Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhury was an eminent personality known for his contributions to Indian football and his patronage of sports.
 
• The Santosh Trophy is an annual Indian football tournament contested by states and government institutions.
 
• It was originally organized to promote football at the grassroots level and is considered one of the most prestigious state-level competitions in India.
 
• Initially, the tournament featured teams representing various states in India, encouraging regional talent to compete and gain recognition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sir Henry Mortimer Durand**:

 
 
• He was a British diplomat and civil servant, best known for the Durand Line Agreement of 1893, which established the border between British India and Afghanistan.
 
• The Durand Line remains a significant geopolitical boundary between modern-day Pakistan and Afghanistan.
 
• He played no role in Indian football or sports development, making this option unrelated to the Santosh Trophy.
 
 
 
• **Syed Abdul Rahim**:
 
 
• Syed Abdul Rahim was an iconic Indian football coach and manager who led the Indian national team during its golden era in the 1950s and 1960s.
 
• Under his guidance, India won the 1951 and 1962 Asian Games gold medals in football.
 
• Although he made significant contributions to Indian football, the Santosh Trophy was not named after him.
 
 
 
• **Sailen Manna**:
 
 
• Sailen Manna was a legendary Indian footballer and captain of the national team in the 1950s.
 
• He is regarded as one of the finest defenders in Indian football history and was awarded the Padma Shri for his contributions to the sport.
